title: Watchtower ops — weekly runlog and handoff notes (2029-12-12)
content:
TL;DR:
- P99 latency spike on hosted API during patch rollout (Dec 11 23:18–23:42 UTC) — mitigated by temporary rollback and autoscaler tuning.
- Small memory leak traced to local KV-cache eviction in dedicated pool; fix staged in infra branch (PR 2147).
- Error budget burn accelerated for embeddings route (2.8% burn this week) — watch alerts and hold canary for next 48h.

Incidents (short-form)
1) Incident: hosted-api latency spike (INC-SRE-2029-12-11-01)
   - Severity: Sev2 (customer-impacting degraded latency)
   - Timeline: 2029-12-11 23:18 UTC first spike, mitigation applied 23:28 UTC, partial rollback complete 23:36 UTC, full recovery 23:42 UTC.
   - Observables: P99 CPU on model-host nodes rose from 62% -> 89%, request queue length increased ~6x, per-request KV-cache miss rate spiked.
   - Root cause hypothesis: new kernel selection path (autoscheduler v3.2) mis-tuned for short-seq traffic; combined with autoscaler cooldowns prevented fast scale-up.
   - Immediate mitigations: rolled back autoscheduler config to v3.1 candidate, increased autoscaler max-inflight temporarily, bumped node pool warm count.
   - Owner: Diego Alvarez.
   - Next steps: postmortem draft (SRE-7829), regression test added to staging perf-suite, runbook note to add preflight canary for scheduler changes.

2) Incident: dedicated pool memory creep (INC-SRE-2029-12-10-02)
   - Severity: Sev3 (internal capacity pressure)
   - Timeline: gradual over 48h, alerted 2029-12-10 11:03 UTC when one node OOM-killed.
   - Observables: resident set consistently drifting upward on one host class; heap growth correlated with rare eviction code path (local KV-cache eviction on quantized models).
   - Root cause: bug in eviction pointer arithmetic during heavy prefix caching.
   - Immediate mitigations: drained affected nodes, reverted recent cache-change commit, landed hotfix in branch and deploying canary.
   - Owner: Priya Kapoor.
   - Next steps: merge hotfix PR (GH PR 2147), add e2e memory smoke test to release pipeline, schedule dedicated pool soak for 72h.

3) Alert storm: embeddings route elevated errors (ALERT-EBDG-1212)
   - Severity: Sev3->monitoring (high error budget burn rate)
   - Observables: 5xx rate on /v1/embeddings up from 0.02% -> 0.9% during weekday peak; increased latency on upstream fe-cache requests.
   - Mitigations: scaled embedding workers by +15% for peak window, enabled extra request logging for failing payloads.
   - Owner: Noah Kim.
   - Next steps: triage logs for payload patterns, add parameterized load test for typical embedding sizes, consider temporary rate-limiting guard for anomalous clients.

SLO snapshot (end-of-week)
- Hosted API availability (global): 99.94% (target 99.95%) — error budget remaining: ~0.35% for month.
- P50/P95/P99 latency (text gen): 18ms / 72ms / 610ms (note P99 elevated due to Wednesday spike).
- Embeddings success rate: 99.10% (target 99.5%) — currently consuming ~55% of monthly error budget.
- Action: Hold non-critical deploys to dedicated/hosted scheduling paths until regression tests pass.

On-call handoff notes (for next shift: 2029-12-13 07:00 UTC)
- Current open tickets: SRE-7829 (latency postmortem, Diego), SRE-7834 (mem leak hotfix validation, Priya), SRE-7837 (embeddings client pattern triage, Noah).
- Pager rules changed temporarily: increased throttle on autoscaler alerts to reduce noise while we iterate on cooldown. See Confluence Watchtower page for details.
- Running experiments: autoscheduler v3.2 canary limited to region-us-west-2; disable flag: feature.autoscheduler.v3.2=false.
- Hot resources: dedicated-pool-42 in draining state (expected empty by 2029-12-13 02:00 UTC).
- Recommended actions for next oncall: keep an eye on node warm-count metrics, watch P99 tail for hosted-api and embeddings, escalate to platform on any eviction/OOM recurrence.

Runbook and process gaps observed
- No preflight canary step exists for kernel selection/autoscheduler changes — add a small traffic canary and perf-checklist.
- Memory smoke tests missing for quantized-model eviction path.
- Alert thresholds for embeddings route are too tight for transient client spikes (leads to noisy paging).

Planned maintenance & deploy windows
- Short maintenance: infra: autoscaler cooldown tuning (non-disruptive) — planned 2029-12-14 01:00–02:00 UTC (low risk).
- Larger: staged rollout of kv-cache eviction fix (after PR validation) — target 2029-12-15 canary then 24h slow ramp if no regressions.

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Diego: complete postmortem draft and attach perf graphs (ETA: 2029-12-15).
- Priya: validate memory hotfix in canary and add memory smoke tests to pipeline (ETA: 2029-12-14).
- Noah: triage embeddings failure logs and implement preliminary payload filter (ETA: 2029-12-14).
- Jin: update runbook with autoscheduler canary checklist and flag procedures (ETA: 2029-12-16).
- Maya (owner): coordinate cross-team retro & customer comms for embedded incidents (ETA: 2029-12-18).

Meeting notes (synthesis from sync 2029-12-12 10:00 UTC)
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya, Noah, Jin, Alex R.
Key points:
- Consensus to pause autoscheduler v3.2 rollout until perf-suite completes, add additional monitoring instrumentation.
- Agreement to treat embeddings error budget as a high-priority signal for canary gating.
- Need for clearer escalation path to platform infra for OOMs during draining events.

Misc notes / notes-to-self
- TODO: create a small Grafana dashboard tile that shows per-scheduler-version tail latency side-by-side.
- Reminder: forward customer-facing incident notes to CS for top-20 customers after postmortem.
- Quick test: run mem-probe script against quantized models with prefix-caching enabled.

Useful links (quick refer)
- Postmortem draft (JIRA SRE-7829)
- Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2147
- Slack thread: #sre-watchtower: thread/req-ftp-33
- Runbook: Confluence /display/SRE/Watchtower+Runbook

End of weekly runlog.

— Maya C.
